utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted by Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution, to everyone in and around the courtroom. I'm Vasvija Vidovic. With me is Mr. Nicholas Robson, representing General Rasim Delic, and with us is Lana Deljkic, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, sir. Just to remind you that you made a declaration at the beginning of your testimony yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You are still bound by that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, you were --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hajderhodzic. I hope you are rested and we can continue.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we spoke about the Arabs that were in the territory of the Zavidovici municipality, and that's where we stopped. Now I would like to ask you about something that I think you may be able to assist us with. Am I right if I believe that the El Mujahedin unit was not the only Arab unit in 1995 that took part in the fighting in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there were various Arab groups?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were many people. I didn't know them, but they walked around.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were criminal gangs among them, such as, for instance, Hamdala's group, and you, as an intelligent officer, probably heard about them?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Vozuca, in the Farz operation, the El Mujahedin was not the only group that participated in combat operations, I mean, not the only Arab group; is it so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did you hear about the group of Abu Zubeir [Realtime trascript read in error "Abu Zabaydah"] Al Halili?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Hamdala's group and Abu Zubeir Al Halili group did not have anything to do with BH Army?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure that the El Mujahedin group had nothing to do with the BH Army and least of all the other ones that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, every time I say "Abu Zubeir," the transcript says "Abu Zabaydah." I'm talking about Abu Zubeir. We had this problem in all the transcripts, in particular the transcript of Ali Ahmed Al Hamed [phoen], so I'll make an official motion to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you understand that I'm talking about Abu Zubeir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't have any knowledge of Abu Zubeir's group participating in fighting in Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything about that. Fine. You saw some documents where a mention is made of the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yet you never saw any documents where the Abu Zubeir Al Halili's group is mentioned in the context of the 35th Division in any way?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure of that, I never saw anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the same goes for Hamdala's group?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, these units, I mean Abu Zubeir Al Halili and his units and Hamdala, were not supposed to take part in the combat operations in Operation Farz, they were not in the plans?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let me now ask you something about the prisoners of war. This is something that you testified about yesterday. You will agree with me that Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did have regulations in place about the treatment of prisoners of war at the time of the events that you testified about yesterday, so this is 1995?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Personnel in units knew the definition of the term "prisoner of war"; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At least the officers were aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at document D513. D513.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you the instruction on the application of the Rules of International Law of War in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you agree with me that it says here that these instructions were issued on the 5th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at page 2 in the Bosnian version. That would be page 4 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus -- and could we look at the right-hand side of the text? I'm interested in Articles 20 and 21, and if we could scroll down the English version for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. I'm interested in the provisions in Article 20 and 21. I would now like to ask you to read those provisions to yourself. Do you agree with me that these instructions allowed the questioning of prisoners of war on information of military nature, but no pressure was to be exerted?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, in the field, were aware of how the prisoners of war were to be treated?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you please look at Article 21. You agree with me that it stipulates that prisoners of war should be protected from bombing and other threats, and that they should be provided with foods, clothes, footwear and care, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you and all your fighters were aware of these rules?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at Article 19, para 2. It says it is forbidden to apply measures of oppression against prisoners of war. They must be treated in a humane way, without using violence, offence or threats in full respect of their personality and honour. These are all the provisions that were familiar?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be Exhibit 557.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at Exhibit 444. This exhibit was shown to the witness yesterday by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness please look at page 8 of the Bosnian version, and that would be page 21 in the English version of this document. You remember, sir, that you saw this order yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an order of the 18th of July, 1995. It says here in the right-hand corner: "Proljece 1995"; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus on item 11.4. We can see it in the English version, too. Could you please look at it. You can see here that the treatment of prisoners of war is regulated in this item; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that the regulations reached the units, the instruction on the treatment of prisoners of war reached the units, and it is obviously used in the orders where the treatment of prisoners of war is regulated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see here that the centre for prisoners of war is determined here. That was the Military Police Company in Zavidovici; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the witness please look at the last page of this document. That's page 34 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 16.12. Yes, fine, excellent. Also in the English version. Thank you very much. Could you please look at this item. This was shown to you by the Prosecutor yesterday. You can see here that the commander, Colonel Hasanagic, defines the location where the prisoners of war are to be gathered, and he also stipulates that the questioning and further care of the prisoners of war is within the purview of the intelligence and security organs of the 35th Division. This is what your commander stipulated; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And do you agree that this is the reason why you went there in the field, to have a look at those prisoners of war, once you received reports that they were there?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, surely, for certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You testified that you saw some of those prisoners on the 21st of July, 1995. You testified that you saw Dr. Sikanic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were accompanied by Mr. Fadil Imamovic from the security organ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you demanded that the members of the detachment untie the hands of the prisoner, to untie him so that you could talk to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that he refused to do so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you demand to take over the prisoners at that time?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that Mr. Imamovic made that demand.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they did not allow you to take over the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you, you described the inhumane treatment of this prisoner of war. This is what you saw?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any injuries on the face or the body of that prisoner?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you something about the further actions taken in respect to those prisoners of war. In your testimony yesterday, you said that you were not sure whether you had reported to the superior command about the state of that prisoner of war; in other words, that he had been tied up in an inappropriate, inhumane manner? Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you said that you were not sure whether you had reported this to the 3rd Corps Command; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to go through your reports from that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be shown D514. Witness -- could the witness please just see the date on this document. You see that the date is -- a document from the intelligence organ -- is that okay? May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry. I thought -- I didn't think you heard me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a document from the intelligence section of the 35th Division, dated the 21st of July, 1995. Could we scroll down a little bit so that we see the signature on it. It appears to be your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to explain the following to us: Do you agree with me that the information about the prisoners of war, if any, should be contained in this report, where -- under the heading "Losses of the Aggressor Forces" or "Successes of our Units"?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So could you please look at this section of this document?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that it is mentioned here that about 50 aggressor soldiers were killed, and they were mostly on our side? Do I understand it correctly that this means that the bodies of the dead aggressor soldiers are on the BH side?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the gist of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Could you please look at the other remarks made here. Do you agree with me that there is no information about the prisoners of war for that date?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be Exhibit 558.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at D515. This is a document -- I don't know if you see it, sir. While we're waiting for the English version to come up, I want to state for the record that this is a document from the intelligence section of the 35th Division, dated the 22nd of July, 1995. It was sent to the 3rd Corps Command, the Intelligence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that? Witness, now I would like to ask you -- in fact, if we could just scroll down so that the witness sees the bottom part of the document. Could we do the same thing in English, please. Witness, I'm going to ask you the same thing. Could you please look at this document, at the sections where it says "The successes of our units"," or losses, or in fact anywhere in this document, is any mention made in any way of the prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're not mentioned at all, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a good look, sir. Could document -- were you able to read the document?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree with me that nothing is said about prisoners of war, in particular of any mistreatment of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the next page of this document. That's page 3 in the English version, page 2 in the Bosnian version. Yes, fine, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, sir, that you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be given an exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be Exhibit 559.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, the names that are mentioned here towards the end of the document, who were these people? Just ascertain that they were not prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the intelligence report indicates contacts with the personnel of the international organisations. The way I understand this document is these are representatives of the international organisations who were active in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Witness, could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Those are the names of the people that we were in contact with.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And representatives of international organisations?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their affiliations, their duties, and all other important information is stated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm asking because it says that they were arrested for apparently filming the territory in the Misurici sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that their arrest has nothing to do with the prisoners of war; this was all about the operation of the international organisations in this area and that their arrest is described on the other page of this document? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Could the witness please look at D516.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this is again a document from the Command of the 35th Division, the intelligence section, dated the 23rd of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document is entitled "Daily Intelligence Report," and could we just scroll down the document so that we see the signature. Do you agree with me that this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but could you please just let me look at the initials here to the right? Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. As far as I can see, it says "FR," but at any rate, could you please look at this document again. Could you please look at this section where it says: "The success of our units," and the document again, looking at any information -- looking for any information about the prisoners of war and their mistreatment, in particular?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no information about any of that here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you. Could this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 560.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, these documents are obviously important evidence, and so I wonder if you would be kind enough to also ask your witness if there, in these reports, is any mention of the El Mujahid Detachment, because somebody will have to ask these questions anyway, and so you might as well do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you heard His Honour. When we look at these documents, could you please pay attention to whether the El Mudjahedin Detachment is mentioned there? Could you please look at this document. Is there any mention of the prisoners of war or of the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no mention is made of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, at least not in my reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we're talking about the reports that you're looking at now.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can we please have a number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it not a document that is already 560?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is quite possible. Thank you. Could we please have D517. This is a poor copy, Your Honour. We shall try and provide the witness with a hard copy instead. Just for the record and before the witness receives a copy:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a document produced by the 3rd Corps Command, Intelligence Department? Of course, Witness, I'm not going to ask you anything about how this document was produced, simply because you're not supposed to know anything about that. I will merely be asking you questions about its substance, about what it suggests. Do you see that it was sent to the General Staff of the Army, the Intelligence Administration; right? In the lower right-hand corner, you can see that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the 23rd of July. Can you please go to page 3 of this document, of the Bosnian version, page 4 in English. You see Amir Abazovic's signature there? Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I know that man.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. He worked in the intelligence body of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please go back to page 2 of this document, which is page 3 in the English. Page 2, page 3, the portion in relation to the successful operations carried out by our fighters. Can you please read carefully. Your Honours, it's the first paragraph on this page. About midway down the page, there is a reference to the aggressor having suffered about 150 casualties, a lot of materiel and technical equipment was seized, 11 Muslims were captured who were doing some engineers work in the area of the 1st Prnjavor Brigade. Do you agree that on this day, the 23rd of July, the Intelligence Department of the 3rd Corps obviously had nothing about any POWs of the Army of Republika Srpska, especially not any sort of mistreatment of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a quick look for any reference to the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please receive a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 561, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D518. For the record, this is a 35th Division document, Intelligence Department, dated the 24th of July, 1995. Could we please go to page 2 of this document, which is page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think you signed this document; didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to page 1 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I'll be asking you to read sections of this document where you think any information on POWs might appear, or the El Mudjahedin Detachment. If we could please scroll down for the witness to inspect the document. Have a look at this bit that says: "Losses" and: "The success of our units."

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing about POWs then being mistreated, nothing about the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 562, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now put this document away, and let us please show D519 to the witness. Before the English shows up, this is a 35th Division document, Intelligence Department, dated the 25th of July, 1995. This is another daily intelligence report. Can we please scroll down, first of all, so that the witness might be able to look at the bottom half of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look, sir. See if you can find anything on this page, such as what I've been asking you about, Republika Srpska POWs or the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any such information in this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is no information here on POWs or the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree, there is none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 563.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you that you said that you found out about the war prisoners, prisoners of war, in July, soon after their arrest, and you saw them very soon after their arrest. I have now shown you a whole sequence of documents that you sent on to the 3rd Corps. You agree, there is no information about POWs in any of them? What I'm putting to you now is this: I'm putting to you that this information does not exist in July or in August 1995, it's not to be seen in any of your reports. Do you accept that, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you accept that you never passed on any information concerning any mistreatment of POWs to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what we've seen, that would be the inference, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I wish to ask you something about POWs in the September operation known as "Operation Farz."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before you move on to the next subject, I think the question hangs on everybody's lips, why the witness didn't include any information about the prisoners of war to the higher echelons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you've heard this question. Can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've answered this one already. It was in one of my previous answers. I believe that if I had no intelligence of any relevance, I shouldn't make things up. My duty was to inform on the enemy, their forces, their deployment, that sort of thing. I had with me a man who was in charge of receiving these and securing them, and I thought he would do things his own way, because there were people in our territory. These are all the reasons that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think you said that you wouldn't pass on any information unless you had facts to base that information on, and it would seem to me that having seen, with your own eyes, the mistreatment of at least one prisoner of war, possibly three prisoners of war, during your short visit in Livade, that would suggest that evidence had been offered to you of mistreatment and that this information would have been relevant for the 3rd Corps intelligence to be made aware of. So, again, the question is: Why is there no mention of what you had seen, yourself, with your own eyes, in your reports from these days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I believed there was no need for me to address this issue. I believed that we were a team and that everyone would do their job; security would do their job, I would do the intelligence bit. I didn't think at all that our competences should in any way coincide or overlap. Both documents went the same way. They were sent to the division commander and then on to the higher-level command, which was the corps command in this case. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And did you not see your colleague's report or inquire whether he had included this information in his report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't see it, but I had every confidence that the man would get the job done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if I may just ask, follow the same point from a slightly different angle. I accept and I understand your explanation, given what you told us yesterday, that you deal with intelligence and Mr. Imamovic dealt with security. What I would like you to explain is why, then, today, at page 7, line 23, you answered Madam Vidovic's question by a "yes," where she asked you: "Fine. And do you agree that this is the reason why you went there in the field, to have a look at those prisoners of war, once you received reports that they were there?" Now, if you look at what was said previously, it suggested that you are accepting that the responsibility for prisoners of war is yours, and therefore you've got to pass that information on about them. I can't understand why you said "yes" to that answer -- to that question, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's quite difficult for me to interpret the legal implications of a single word or a comma. It is quite obvious that I will have to focus more on the questions. But there is one thing that is certain. Somebody tells you to go and have a look at something, what that means to me is I should go and do my job, see the people, do what my job entails. That's all. And that's why I said that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem is before that question, Madam Vidovic explained to you, she says: "Okay. Could you please look at item 6.12"? Yes, fine, excellent. Also in the English version, thank you very much: "Could you please look at this item? This was shown to you by the Prosecutor yesterday. You can see here that the commander, Colonel Hasanagic, defines the location where the prisoners of war are to be gathered, and he also stipulates that the questioning and further care of the prisoners of war is within the purview of the intelligence and security organs of the 35th Division. This is what your commander stipulated; is that so?" Now, that is obviously contrary to what you told us, because the care of the prisoners of war, according to your testimony, is not within the purview of Intelligence, it is within the purview of Security. You didn't correct her there and say, "Sorry, madam, the purview of Security but not the purview of Intelligence." And then when she asks you the next question, which is where I started, you say, yes, that's the reason you went there, because the care of prisoners was within your purview. That's why you went to Livade. And you say, "Yes." That's what I don't understand, but I hear what you said. Do you have any answer? It was not just one word and you can answer " ..." She explained clearly to you what she wanted to get from you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I'd explained that already. I don't know whether we understand each other well. But what this order says is intelligence and security organ, the intelligence organ, and I've said this once already, is hereby allowed access, but this does not make the intelligence organ responsible for the implementation of this. The intelligence organ, I talked about how it was organised. They didn't have the instruments to protect, to take in, to do anything at all concerning POWs. All it could do was talk. That's how it was organised. What this order does is it allows me to interview them, but nothing more than that. Maybe the wording is slightly awkward, the wording of this order, awkward. Well, it's written the way it's written, but all it does is it allows me to interview them, nothing more than that. Quite literally, the intelligence organ had no instruments, in a manner of speaking, to do anything else but simply to interview these men. That was all. Everything else fell under the purview of another body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the witness could please look at 556.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is 556, Madam Vidovic? Is it a "D" document or is it an exhibit? An exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit, yes. For the record, before the English version appears, this is a document produced by the Command of the 35th Division, dated the 24th of August, 1995. F-95, that's what it says, which means that it has to do with Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that was shown to you yesterday by the Prosecutor. I believe this is a document that you signed about the command of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, and there's something I wish to ask you about it. You explained yesterday that you had received orders to forward this document to them as well, and this is what I wish to ask you something about. You never received any intelligence at all from the El Mudjahedin Detachment that would seem to follow from this order of yours; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please go to page 3 of this document, page 3 of the Bosnian and page 6 of the English. Could you please try to focus on item 6. Do you agree that it is hereby being ordered to the detachment to take POWs and refugees to the provisional custody centre of the Military Police? What I want to know is: Did the detachment, in fact, comply with this order? Did they ever bring over to you any POWs?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Your Honours, I want to show a different document now. This is P02568. 2568.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You'll agree with me that this was produced by the 3rd Corps Command, the Intelligence Department, and the date is the 11th of September, 1995. This is a warning. It is submitted to the intelligence organs of unit commands; am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is not a long document. Can you please read it. You will agree with me, won't you, that the document was signed by Captain Edin Music; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know who he is; right? He was your superior, your superior in terms of subordination in the 3rd Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the intelligence organ of the 3rd Corps, your superior, that is, is here warning you about your responsibility of submitting intelligence reports?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the very last sentence of this document. It reads: "The intelligence organ of the 35th Division is to put together all of the above information in relation to all of its units, including the El Mudjahedin Detachment and the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion." Is that what the warning states?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, although it reads above that the report of the 35th Division was submitted, but without these units, so the warning is about retrieving information in relation to these two units as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the El Mudjahedin Detachment did not forward any information to you, so you, in turn, were not able to forward any information to them; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this document was to contain something else. I should have been given an instrument which would have allowed me to retrieve information from them. I'd accepted this at the time. I heard it and soon forgot about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What is it you accepted and heard and soon forgot about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the order that came from the superior command. This was down the technical line of command, and it was telling me to obtain information from the El Mujahedin Department and submit information to them as soon as I received it. I had no way of retrieving information from those people. I couldn't extract information from people, could I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand you to be saying you saw this order, you accepted it, and you just forgot about it? That's how you dealt with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, maybe there is too much haste in my answers, too much haste. I got this order, I received it. I'm sure that I received it. This sort of order could not have bypassed me, no way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You forgot about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to make a bit of a joke, a bit of a prank, maybe change the tone to a more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just advise you, we are not joking here. We are very serious. Okay? We are very serious; right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I won't try this sort of thing again. Why did I say this? Simply because of this. This was the situation: Someone orders you to do something, they must give you a means of doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just tell you, quite apart from joking, I must remind you of the declaration you made at the beginning and that I reminded you at the beginning of your testimony today. Now, let me just -- you said you were joking. Putting jokes aside, do I then understand you to say you saw the report, and because you were not given any instrument to get the information from the El Mudjahedin Detachment with, you then decided to do nothing about that report; is that the sum total of your testimony on this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point is this: I couldn't do anything. I didn't know who to turn to in order to retrieve information or reports from the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I'll ask you to listen to the question. I'm not asking you what you could do. I'm asking you what you did. You then did not do anything about it. You did not try to get any information from the El Mudjahedin Detachment because you had no instrument to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You know, we shouldn't be fighting about a simple question and a simple answer. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 564, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me go back to your evidence yesterday. In response to the Prosecutor's questions about the prisoners of war in September 1995, that's in relation with Operation Farz, you said, and I'm referring to page 52 of the transcript, lines 3 through 7, Your Honours, that you received a report of about 50 to 60 captured members in the vicinity of the village of Kesten. This was from the Gostovici Battalion. You remember you said that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you clarified that you received this report from the assistant who was at the forward command post at Klek. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I want to ask you: You did not have many assistants at that time. Who was this assistant? Could you please tell us his name, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, that was at that time Munis Camdzic [phoen]. I think his initials that are listed there are "MC." He was at the forward command post at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to clarify something. I don't understand what you mean when you say that the initials were there at the beginning. Did you see this report during the war, and then you were able to see the initials, or was this document shown to you recently?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall every single event, there were so many events, and I can't recall every single document, every single document, but I think that Munis Camdzic was there at the forward command post. I'm not sure who actually drafted the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you bring up the initials "MC" now?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the text is drafted by the person whose initials are listed first.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm trying to find out how you obtained this information. In other words, you saw a written report of some kind; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see this written report?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the written report on that day, the day that is indicated on the document, and this document that I received, I did not change, I did not amend in any way, I did not add anything. I simply forwarded this document on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see this document as you were preparing for your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecutor show it to you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you the following question: You mentioned this report yesterday, but you will recall that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would ask that Defence counsel clarify the written -- what written document the witness is receiving to when he said that he saw a written document in preparation for his testimony here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me try. I'm very much interested in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what written report did you see as you were being prepared for this testimony? Who drafted it and who was it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear someone say "receive." I didn't receive anything. I was only able to look at things. There were many documents. But if we're talking about the document that I signed and that was sent to the 3rd Corps, that was the document where mention is made of the captured personnel, I don't know. At any rate, I saw this document. Whether it was here or in Sarajevo, I don't know, but I saw it. I really don't know where it was that I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, don't discuss documents in general now. I asked you about a report that you received from your subordinate. Did you see such a report, a written report?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure, but I'm sure that I saw it in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. You are asked to not overlap, please. Remember, you're speaking the same language, and before either of you speaks, there must be interpretation. So you've got to give time for that interpretation to be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you also saw a document in which you report this to someone else, that you report about those prisoners in September; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know where it was, because there are so many documents, so many things, and I really don't remember what I saw, what I didn't see. But I am sure that I saw this either in Sarajevo or in here. This is a little -- I have a little bit better recollection.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But we're always talking about the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we're talking about the Office of the Prosecutor either here or in Sarajevo, because I didn't meet with anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, now I would like to ask you the following question: You remember that you gave a statement to the Prosecutor in April 2007; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the investigator asked you many questions, detailed questions about the taking of those prisoners? I'm talking about the 61 prisoners that were taken. Now, let me remind you of the facts, and I'm referring to tape 9395, page 1 and 2 in the Bosnian version. That would be pages 2 and 3 in the English version. So I'm talking about the transcript of the statement given to the OTP investigators. That's tape 9395, pages 1 and 2 in the Bosnian version and pages 2 and 3 in the English version. The OTP investigator showed you a document originating from the 328th Brigade, indicating that this brigade captured 61 enemy soldiers and 3 women, ethnic Serbs. The investigators -- the investigator allowed you to read this document in its entirety and asked you the following, I quote: "Fine. Did you hear about this number of prisoners taken on that day?" Your answer is: "No, no." And then another question by the investigator: "How come that you didn't hear about those prisoners, because after all, this is part of your area of responsibility?" And then on the same two pages, there was an altercation between you and the OTP investigator, and in lines 26 through 29, you say: "It is possible that this information bypassed the Division and that it went straight up to the Corps level." And then further down on the same page, when the investigator asked you the next question: "And you definitely did not receive the information about this number?" Your answer is: "No, no." So now I want to ask you: How come, sir, that in April 2007, just a few months ago, you were so certain that you had never received this information about the prisoners, yet a little while ago you remembered not only the report but you remembered the initials that were listed on this report? So what refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I saw this report somewhere, but I really don't know about this report. The reports went to the forward command post. Through the reports, I was supposed to be told about this and I was supposed to sign this report. And if this kind of a report was sent on, I signed it as is, in its raw, unedited form. And why did I say that the initials are important? The person who was the assistant is listed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you about the facts, not about the reports. How is it possible that mere months ago, you were so certain that you did not receive any information about the number of prisoners, yet yesterday you -- your testimony was different? Why is that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I probably saw the report somewhere. I really don't know. I don't know what is -- in fact, it is difficult for me to say, because in an informal -- there was an informal conversation in Sarajevo. Now, whether it was informal or formal, I -- I never received any copies of this interview. I was never able to read what I said and how and why, which would refresh my memory. I simply didn't consider it to be all that important, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Please, the way I understand you, I showed you portions of your statement in February 1997. This is on record.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]

I don't remember what it is that I said, and I cannot now tell you with any certainty I said this, I said that, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but I showed you parts of what you said. Do you agree that you said what I just quoted to you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're reading from the transcript, then that's probably what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to show the witness a few other documents that I consider to be very relevant. I will take maybe about 15 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 2007, or April 2007. April 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11:00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

Of course, it was impossible to have them translated, so I will be showing the witness those documents. And if you allow me to proceed in that manner, the documents will be tendered into evidence the moment we receive the translations. I have two -- or rather two of these documents have been traps translated, but the rest, three or four other documents, we don't have the translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can have the interpreters interpret what you are going to be doing with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for the record, Witness, please follow what I'm saying. Do you agree that it says here: "35th Division Command, Intelligence Section"? utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC

utterances.text: Sir, now I would like you to confirm the following: This is a report. The headline is "Features of the Combat Operations and status of the Aggressor"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll down a little bit further. utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Successes of our units. The successful actions of our units continue in combat operations --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go slow.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please read what it says under: "Losses"?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the course of combat operations, the 1st Srbac and the 4th --" or rather --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read it?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 4th Ozren Light Brigade were completely routed. For the time being, we are unable to provide accurate information about the aggressor losses, and we will submit this information in an interim report."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the time being, we're unable to give you accurate information about the aggressor losses, and we will submit this information in an interim report."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness -- or rather could we just scroll up the document so that we see the beginning of this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would just like you to look at the number of this document. Do you agree that this is 09/109-101-255/95, and I want you to retain in your memory the number "255/95" so that we can keep the sequence of your report in mind.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this report, there is nothing that would have to do with the prisoners of war or any personnel that was captured at all?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.text: The El Mudjahedin Detachment is not mentioned at all?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please check that? Could we have another look at page 2? Could you please zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there is a conclusion here, and no mention is made of any prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Or the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Thank you very much. Could this document be given an exhibit number?

utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 565, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be shown D539. Could you please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this is a document from the 35th Division Command, its intelligence section, dated the 12th of September, 1995? And now I want to ask you the following: You saw that the number on the previous report was "255/95", so do you agree that this is the next report that you sent in, that was "256/95"?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that again it was sent urgently to the Intelligence Department of the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please look at page 2 of this document, Your Honours, because I want to look at the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, do you agree that this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Could we please look at page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that we have the same format? The first item is features of the combat operations and the aggressor status in the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have the description of the attacks launched by the aggressor forces, then the concentration and the regrouping of aggressor forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then we have the use of the aggressor artillery?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document -- could we scroll down a little bit for the witness to be able to read this section that's entitled "The successes of our units," and then further down again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Witness, let me ask you, could you please read it out slowly so that the interpreters can keep up?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the offensive operations, the joint units of the 35th Division inflicted losses on the aggressor." As far as the personnel is concerned, about 400 to 420 soldiers were killed, and a large number of the soldiers were injured seriously or they received minor injuries. A T-55 tank was destroyed, another was captured. A self-propelled weapon, 57/2, was destroyed, and a 30/2 Praga was captured. A large number of motor vehicles was destroyed, in brackets "10 motor vehicles," and at least six vehicles were captured, and they were immediately put to use. The units of the 35th Division routed the 1st Srbac Brigade and elements of the 14th Serbian Light Brigade, which is formed of the elements of units that are part of the 1st Corps. And this is now illegible. And some other units. Both command posts of those brigades were captured, and so were their depots. The aggressor destroyed some of the equipment and materiel by blowing up some of the depots. Weapons such as mortars, antiaircraft guns and machine-guns were destroyed after the enemy forces were routed because they could not be carried. I don't know, I guess that's what it says, "carried." The exact information about the captured equipment and materiel is still not available, but we are now gathering information. Combat operations continue in the sector of Radalovo Brdo on the axis towards the village of Karacici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could we scroll the document down a little bit further."Other Observations." Do you agree with me that now this is about NATO air strikes, that it has nothing to do --

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it says here both command posts were captured. What does that mean, men or command posts?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the command posts were taken. They had been abandoned, left behind. This is a reference to the command post as a facility, not actual men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Do you agree that in this document, there is nothing about POWs?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be Exhibit 566.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D540. I think there is actually an English translation of this document. For the record, Your Honours, before the English appears on our screens, this is a document of the Intelligence Department of the 35th Division, dated the 13th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please have a look at the number, the same number you looked at a while ago. It used to be "256/95". Is this not "257/95", your next report?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, could we please turn to the next page, or rather there is no next page. Can we just see this portion of the document and look at the signature, please. In the Bosnian, this is page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now, could we please look at the portion of the document that says -- could you please look at the document in its entirety first, and then if page 1 could be displayed for the Chamber, page 1 of the English version. Yes. Can we please zoom in on the portion that says: "Successes of our units"?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, look closely at that paragraph, and if we could please zoom in on "Conclusions." If we could scroll the Bosnian down a little. Thank you. The English, too, this portion, just for the witness to see, the entire lower half of the page. There, right. Have you looked at it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is no reference whatsoever about between 50 and 60 POWs?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, no reference to the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 567, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this one away. The next document is D541. Your Honours, I think this is another document that has been translated. If we could please zoom in on this so we can see the date and the document number. For the record, this is a document of the Command of the 35th Division, Intelligence Department, and the number is 258/95, which is the next number in the sequence that we've been looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 14th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please again go through the document and focus on the paragraph that says -- well, actually, look at the document in its entirety. Any reference whatsoever that you notice to POWs or the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could just please scroll down, look at the rest of the document, and then turn the page to see whether there's anything there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Other Observation," you see that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next page, please, just to look at the signature.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, again, no reference to POWs; you agree?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 568, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now D542. Could we please zoom in on the upper half of the page in the Bosnian so that we can see the date and the number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the Command of the 35th Division, Intelligence Department. The number is 259/95, the next number in the sequence; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 15th of September, submitted to the Command of the 3rd Corps, Intelligence Department; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the substance of this document. Your Honours, we have no English translation for this one. I will be asking the witness to look at the portion that says: "Successes of our units." First of all, Witness, do you agree that the upper half of the document describes the concentration and regrouping by the aggressor forces; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then the use of artillery by the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Successes of our units," and then if you can read slowly, please -- no, no, no, this is not the portion. If you could scroll down and zoom in, please. That's it. Can you read this, Witness, slowly for the benefit of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Our forces continue successfully building up on their initial success after routing the front line or the front end of the aggressor and taking the Blizna facility or feature, Dolac village, and Karacic. "Information on other observations. Civilians were noticed moving en masse from Bagatic village towards Jablanica village. Increased traffic in territory under the control of the HVO during the night."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please scroll down slightly to see what it says under the heading "Conclusions."

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Conclusions on the features and condition of the aggressor forces and combat operations in the area of responsibility. The aggressor -- minor firing by artillery on the town."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Maglaj and Zavidovici, in the evening hours, there were no new entries by the aggressor forces to the Ozren area. After routing the aggressor's front end and the advance of our forces on Maglaj town, the aggressor still unable to consolidate their ranks. Our forces are still building on their initial success."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is your signature; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this was a report in reference to the 15th of September, 1995. There is no reference to POWs, is there?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 569 [Realtime transcript read in error "568"], Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, a correction in the transcript. 569.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I've been showing you documents up to the 15th of September. I am putting to you that there is not a single report that you produced until the end of September 1995 where you mentioned this information that you spoke about, between 50 and 60 POWs. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "POWs," I mean soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska whom you say you heard had been captured.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never mentioned those in your reports to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Based on this, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, Mr. Hajderhodzic. It is quite clear, after all, that you had some authority, you say; it was the Military Security Service that had some powers over the prisoners, but would you accept that they were another source of intelligence for you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you knew about those POWs at the time, would it not have been a logical move on your part to go and look for them and try to get some information?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been a logical move, but the situation being what it was, the information would no longer have mattered, at least not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in relation to Operation Farz, the corps ordered that POWs should, first and foremost, be interviewed by intelligence officers before they are taken over by security officers?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree. That was the way it was meant to be. First, you get intelligence officers to interview them, with the assistance of the security service. Intelligence officers are the first to access prisoners and the first to interview them. That's the way it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you never reached this group yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Mr. Menon. Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I want to take you back to -- back to the time you spent in Livade, when you met the POW who you've identified as Mr. Sikanic. Did you spend any time examining Mr. Sikanic for any injuries that he may have suffered?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you recall if Mr. Imamovic spent any time examining Mr. Sikanic for any injuries?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and of course he wasn't qualified to do that sort of thing, examine people for injuries. Nor was I, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during the course of your cross-examination, you've looked at a number of daily intelligence reports that you drafted, and during the course of your direct examination, you had referred to another type of report that you would submit to your superiors, namely, an interim intelligence report.
